steps.name: Wallach
steps.text: Grr... We ended up letting him go.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: He stopped wanting to fight us halfway through.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: You felt it too, didn't you? If he really wanted to kill us, he could've gotten it done.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: He just didn't want to take the time.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: We can't underestimate any of the Siracusan famiglie.

steps.name: Wallach
steps.text: You got one thing wrong.

steps.name: Wallach
steps.text: I've never underestimated any of them.

steps.name: Wallach
steps.text: Every famiglia is my enemy.

steps.name: Wallach
steps.text: Including the Bellones.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Don't you think you're jumping the gun a bit there?

steps.name: Wallach
steps.text: You don't seem surprised.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: You betrayed your own boss. You expect me to believe you'd really go in with us?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: But let me point out, now isn't a good time.
Demetri does not waver in the face of Wallach's sharpened blade, instead turning back to his soldiers.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: What's going on in the city?

steps.name: Bellone Mafioso
steps.text: Nothing good.

steps.name: Bellone Mafioso
steps.text: The famiglie know the secondary core separation sequence started.

steps.name: Bellone Mafioso
steps.text: People are all pretty mad at us and the Saluzzos.

steps.name: Bellone Mafioso
steps.text: Wise guys from the other famiglie are hitting us now too.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: What about the thing I asked you to handle?

steps.name: Bellone Mafioso
steps.text: You were right on the money...

steps.name: Bellone Mafioso
steps.text: The eyes and ears we planted in the other famiglie tell us even though the people are angry at the Bellones and Saluzzos, we aren't their main deal here.

steps.name: Bellone Mafioso
steps.text: All the chaos is down there is exactly what all the famiglie were looking for.

steps.name: Bellone Mafioso
steps.text: Everything Signora Sicilia kept down is bubbling right up to the surface now.

steps.name: Bellone Mafioso
steps.text: There's already fighting over how to divvy up Bellone and Saluzzo assets. And we've got some old grudges out there getting settled.

steps.name: Bellone Mafioso
steps.text: Everyone's hopping in, directly or indirectly.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: (*mutters*) This is exactly what you wanted, huh, Boss?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: (*mutters*) So, you betrayed us after all.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Wallach, you're not an idiot. You get that there's no point to us fighting right now.

steps.name: Wallach
steps.text: Isn't it better to solve the big problems first?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Is this how the Rossatis handled everything back in Columbia?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: You really think you can swallow up Siracusa all on your own?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Pick your friends wisely, Wallach.

steps.name: Wallach
steps.text: Grr.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Don't feel too bad.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Not like I'm jumping for joy to team up with somebody like you.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Where's Leon?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: What? He didn't go back home?

steps.name: Bellone Mafioso
steps.text: Nope. No trace of him anywhere. He's avoiding us, obviously.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Leon, don't tell me...
Demetri takes a deep breath.
There's no point in overthinking things now. He has to face reality.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Now that the famiglie are starting to bite one another, this is the best chance we'll have to take the secondary core area.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: If we're gonna have a future, we'll have to take hold of it first.

steps.name: Saluzzo Mafioso
steps.text: Don Alberto.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: What's the situation?

steps.name: Saluzzo Mafioso
steps.text: It's mayhem out there.

steps.name: Saluzzo Mafioso
steps.text: Wise guys from multiple famiglie are taking advantage of the confusion to attack us, and our soldiers have started to fight back.

steps.name: Saluzzo Mafioso
steps.text: Things have spiraled out of control.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: That's funny. This can't possibly be what that Leontuzzo kid meant.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Now that I think of it, Bernardo, even though Lappland showed up on a whim, you included us in your calculations, didn't you?

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: The ironclad law laid down by Sicilia is crumbling. You've set fire to everything that took decades to make Siracusa what she is.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Is this what you wanted? Why?

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Where's Lappland?

steps.name: Saluzzo Mafioso
steps.text: We haven't been able to reach her since yesterday morning.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Forget it.

steps.name: Saluzzo Mafioso
steps.text: Boss, it's a madhouse out there now. You want us to wait and see if anything changes?

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Hmph. Even if I wanted to keep Famiglia Saluzzo out of this, it's no longer possible.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Bernardo, that old runt. Can't believe he even accounted for all this.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Tell our people out there to come back.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Then, send some of our heavies to the command tower in the secondary core area. The Bellones and Rossatis aren't going to let it go.

steps.name: Saluzzo Mafioso
steps.text: Do you mean—

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: I have no interest in that new city, but I'm not about to let it fall into the hands of those who've betrayed me either.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Padre!

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Leon... I never expected you to find this place.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I happened to recall it from memory.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Since you're here, come take a seat.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I know what you're trying to do here.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Do you?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Since the very beginning, you've wanted to see Siracusa to return to the dark times of sixty years ago.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You want the famiglie all tearing into each other. If Signora Sicilia didn't step in, Siracusa's famiglie may well have mortally wounded each other.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But this time, you want them to break free of Signora Sicilia's chains, and to fight each other until nothing is left.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Hmm... So you understand after all.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: But you didn't come here to confirm your conjecture with me, did you?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: What I want to know is, what exactly made you think this way?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: When I was twenty years old, I was just an ordinary Bellone wise guy.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: They wanted me to rub somebody out, I couldn't pull it off, so I had to flee into a nearby village. I took a new identity and went into hiding.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: I lived there for almost six months.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Nothing particularly notable happened during that time.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: But those six months gave me an entirely new perspective on the country I lived in.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: There is no corner of Siracusa completely free from the influence of the famiglie, but in places like the villages outside the city, the famiglie are just your run-of-the-mill thuggish bullies.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: I found a job as a cobbler, and for that summer, I plied my trade by the side of the road and watched them go about their business.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: In the end, nothing they did impressed me at all. But I will never forget that summer when sweat flowed from my brow like rain.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Leon, whether it's you, me, or any other wise guy, we've all been branded from birth.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: But it was during that summer that I realized—

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Life in Siracusa will continue, even with no famiglie.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: So that's why you helped Lavinia, and didn't mind that the two of us were growing closer...

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You genuinely want to support her cause. Don't you?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: In all honestly, I did want to see the kind of justice she envisions.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Which is why you didn't have insurance for this plan.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You don't need me, Lavinia, or anyone else assuming any of the risk.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You think that when you tear down the famiglie holding down the people, their lives won't be negatively impacted at all.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Absolutely.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But that doesn't go far enough, padre mio.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: It doesn't?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: No. It's far from enough.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Letting the famiglie tear into each other until they've worn themselves out may overturn the existing system.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But that isn't enough to get Siracusa back into the hands of the people.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Are you worried about Signora Sicilia?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: No, what I'm worried about is inertia.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I came to realize something while working as Carracci's assistant.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: The famiglie have had their roots here for thousands of years.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Even if the people reject the famiglie, they have no idea what shape Siracusa might take.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Even after they overthrow the old system, will they manage to build something new?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I don't think so.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: The people will be overwhelmed, not knowing what happened. All they'll know is that their house has suddenly collapsed.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: And when they go to build on top of those ruins, they'll build what amounts to a famiglia.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Nothing will change at all.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: If we continue down this path, we may bring about a Siracusa without famiglie, for a bit.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But the Siracusa you're dreaming of will never come.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You're dreaming too big, padre mio.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You want to give them your Siracusa, but you never stopped to think if they're willing and able to accept it.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: All we can do is to let everyone out there know what's happening, and involve them in the process.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: That's the only way we can start the conversation on a 'Siracusa without the famiglie.'

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Looks like my son's all grown up.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: I thought you came here for a good, old-fashioned father-son argument.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: I didn't expect you to teach me something.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Padre mio...

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: So, what are you going to do?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I'll go find Lavinia, organize a coalition of non-famiglia forces, and seize control of the secondary core's command tower.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: As long as the new city is under my control, I'll have the advantage.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: As for whether I'll be able to negotiate with Signora Sicilia, or if I'll have to confront her directly, we'll cross that bridge when we come to it.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But no matter what happens, we'll be betraying Demetri, and our whole famiglia.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Do it your way then, Leon.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You were the one who started this whole mess. Don't even think about sitting on the sidelines and leaving everything to me.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Don't worry, I'll catch up with you.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Good.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Don Agenir, I hear you never set foot in church.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: Siracusa doesn't need churches. If we accept the teachings of Laterano, we're doomed to be influenced by their culture.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: In the end, all I can do is choose to distance myself.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: But it's worth making an exception, for a man like you.

steps.name: Bailiff
steps.text: Your Honor, everyone's all here. I've counted over fifty.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: That's a lot less than before.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The people planted in here by the famiglie have all gone back home, haven't they?

steps.name: Bailiff
steps.text: That's right.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Hah. Ironic as that may be, it does save me some effort.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Listen up.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The courts occupy an awkward position in Siracusa.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: We represent the will of Signora Sicilia, to some extent, and in return, gain a certain amount of power.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But this power is not enough for us to fulfill our obligations.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Quite the contrary. In many cases, the power we hold only makes us more aware of how powerless we are in the face of the entities known as famiglie.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: We can neither lower our heads and accept it as most ordinary people can, nor can we truly integrate into these famiglie.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Throughout this process, many of our colleagues have been ostracized, pushed out, or even killed because they could not bear the situation any longer.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: In fact, even if they ended up betraying the law, I would not be in a position to blame them.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The truth is, I'm only where I am today because of my connection to Famiglia Bellone.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You all know what happened, and what is happening out there.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: At first I assumed all I could do is what I always did before.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Pray that the famiglia struggles don't chew through too many common folk, and that Signora Sicilia would come to 'mete out justice' for us in the end.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: However, a brave man told us that he thinks the famiglia system is evil, and that all of this is unjust.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: He wanted to change everything, and so he pinned his hopes on me.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: All of you, just like me, come from outside the famiglia system.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You've all worked with me for so many years, and I believe that among you, there are those who harbor even greater grievances against the famiglie than I, and those who understand the status quo more deeply than I.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Therefore, I would like to ask all of you to help me.
A moment of silence passes.

steps.name: Bailiff
steps.text: What can we even do?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The separation sequence of the new city's core area started not long ago.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: This confirms the conspiracy conjured by the Bellones and Saluzzos, as revealed by Ministro Rubio.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: For the famiglie, this was the spark that ignited new conflict. And for us, it is an opportunity.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The new nomadic city will be our bargaining chip amidst the chaos, whether negotiating with Signora Sicilia, or jockeying for power with the famiglie.
Another moment of silence passes.

steps.name: Bailiff
steps.text: Even with all of us together, we don't have enough people.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I have two reliable friends.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Hello, everyone!

steps.name: Bailiff
steps.text: Cellinia?! Why are you—

steps.name: Bailiff
steps.text: And how come I never heard of another Sankta in Volsinii...?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: All you need to know is that Cellinia and her friend are on our side.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Also, Ministro Rubio left some resources to help me, and I managed to get in touch with them.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: They will assist us.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But, I must be honest with you all.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: This is a perilous road, and I can't guarantee that everyone will survive.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Those who don't want to put their lives on the line are free to leave.

steps.name: Bailiff
steps.text: Even if we succeed, will it really accomplish anything?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I can't promise you it will.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The only thing I can promise... is that I'm willing to give my life for this.
Only thirty-some-odd people remain.
But they have no intention of leaving.

steps.name: Serious Bailiff
steps.text: I should be thanking you for giving me this opportunity, Your Honor.

steps.name: Serious Bailiff
steps.text: I would've gone crazy without you here at the courthouse.

steps.name: Resolute Bailiff
steps.text: I heard the radio broadcast, I knew right away what happened.

steps.name: Resolute Bailiff
steps.text: And honestly, I can't take this anymore.

steps.name: Angry Bailiff
steps.text: Maybe we won't actually be able to do anything in the end, but I at least want those wise guys to know that we're not lumps of finmeat for them to butcher.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Thank you, all of you.

steps.name: Siracusan Official
steps.text: Signorina Lavinia, ready on our end.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: So soon?

steps.name: Siracusan Official
steps.text: Haha, the famiglie are all stirred up now.

steps.name: Siracusan Official
steps.text: They don't usually give the common folk a second look. Even now, they probably don't think we can get in their way at all.

steps.name: Siracusan Official
steps.text: But we have to let them know that they've never really had a hand in running the city.

steps.name: Siracusan Official
steps.text: This town belongs to us.

steps.name: Siracusan Official
steps.text: Take your people and go to the control tower.

steps.name: Siracusan Official
steps.text: We'll use everything at our disposal to hold back the wise guys as best as we can.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Thank you. Do your best.

steps.name: Siracusan Official
steps.text: We're the ones who should be thanking you.

steps.name: Siracusan Official
steps.text: We never took the famiglie head on, and now we're leaving the most dangerous work to you.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I'm ready and willing.

steps.name: Siracusan Official
steps.text: In bocca al lupo.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Crepi.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: You used Carracci as bait, got your own son involved, and even tricked your own associates under the righteous pretense of handling Sicilia, all to muddy the waters of this city.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: You didn't even waver in the face of Saluzzo's lone wolf. Instead, you took that opportunity to drag Saluzzo into the mud with you.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: The high-profile assassination of the Rossati girl was, on one hand, to convince Alberto that he had an ally in you, while on the other hand, serving as an example to the other famiglie.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: You've made full use of Texas as your final card. In Giovanna's hands, the Rossatis were a deadly but hidden saber.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: But in Wallach's hands, they are a savage and ostentatious knife.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: You saw Rubio's connection with Carracci, and even took advantage of his anger. He thought no one knew his self-restraint, he never expected that you had already uncovered him.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: I knew you'd be in town, but I didn't expect you to see through all my plans so easily.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: It is always easier to trace back the steps in retrospect.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: And your plan has already been set in motion. Even if I was able to deduce all this, there is nothing more I can do.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: Even if Sicilia were to pop up right here, right now, even she would be hard-pressed to resolve everything.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: Who would have imagined that the don of the most powerful famiglia would use his own people as bait to bring all the others down with him?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: You don't seem particularly upset about it.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: Sicilia never asked me for a Siracusa that would flourish forever.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: And I was never after wealth or power.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: What you've done undoubtedly breaks the rules that Sicilia established, and so, I really did come to end you.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: But your father-son talk there surprised me.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: Sicilia has never tolerated any disruptions to her order because no one came with an answer that could satisfy her.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: But you, Bernardo, have an excellent son.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: You won't be able to shake apart this society Sicilia built with her own two hands. Not by yourself.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: But, if your son came along with you, then maybe...

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: It wouldn't be completely impossible.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Hahahaha!

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Life is full of surprises.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: I thought I realized my lifelong dream and could die happy today.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Who knew that I'd change my mind, that I'd want to live to see what Leon can do.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: It's too bad.
For a moment, Agenir casts his gaze in the direction of Grey Hall.
Something inhuman is approaching.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: I see, I've heard of this. Is it also a part of your plan?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: It's something that has to be done. That's all.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Please go, Don Agenir.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: This is the price I have to pay.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: So be it.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Just a moment, Reverend.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: Hmm?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Don Agenir, or rather, Padre, I've never prayed to anyone, in my entire life.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: And I don't think I'll find closure with anyone else.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: The Lord can't answer me.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: But right here, I do have some questions only you can answer.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: By all means.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: How did Signora Sicilia feel, when she came back from Laterano?

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: Conflicted.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: She was distressed about the challenges she was to face.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: She was looking forward to the society she was about to create.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: More or less the same as you're feeling right now.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Alright, okay. I know. You be careful too.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: How're Texas n' Exusiai doin'?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Uh, they're with Lavinia right now. Said they were doing her a favor.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: The judge lady, huh? Least she's a bit more put together'n the Bellone family fellers from before.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: Hope nothin' bad happens to 'em.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Giovanna
steps.text: Ugh... Nngh...

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Miss Giovanna! Y-You're awake?!

steps.name: Giovanna
steps.text: I'm... not dead?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: The assassin missed your heart by a couple centimeters, and you pulled through.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: I gotta say, though, it's a good thing you're in such excellent shape. Otherwise, you probably wouldn't have made it.

steps.name: Giovanna
steps.text: Wallach...

steps.name: Giovanna
steps.text: How long was I unconscious for?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: A day.

steps.name: Giovanna
steps.text: I'm guessing a lot has happened over the course of that day.

steps.name: Giovanna
steps.text: Tell me what's going on.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Alright...

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: You're finally here, Don... Or should I say, Zaaro.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Bernardo.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: What are you scheming?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Don't play dumb. I can tell you're in denial about the conclusions you've drawn.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: You dare—

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Why wouldn't I dare?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: You've pushed into me a lifetime of power and betrayal. You're so prideful and arrogant, you never imagined that one day, I could betray you too.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Don't forget, Bernardo, I'm the one who made you everything you are!
A pitch-black mist wraps around Bernardo's neck.
But he pays it no heed.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: You still don't get it, Zaaro.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: The game you Signori dei Lupi are playing means nothing to me.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Siracusa is the absolute limit of your imagination.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: You think that ultimate power is to control a country, multiple countries, or even to subjugate all the lands.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: But I don't think so.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Real power is the power to command an entire epoch.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: In my original plan, Siracusa would fall along with me.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Now, my son has shown me that he sees a bigger picture.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: You should take comfort in that.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Now, take that comfort back to your mountain forest.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: In this round of the game—

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: You... have lost.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: I lost? Hmph. I still have countless ways to—
Il Signore dei Lupi has many ways to control his Fangs.
However, Zaaro immediately notices a trail of blood running from the corner of Bernardo's mouth.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Poison?!

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: You were planning this from the very beginning, weren't you? Bernardo!
Bernardo does not answer. He has already lost the strength to speak.
He simply lifts his head and looks at the wide-open doors of the church.
His gaze passes over flowerbeds, tall buildings, and dark clouds.
Until it finally passes through time itself.
He sees the summer of that year when he, as a cobbler, was sweating profusely beneath the scorching sun.
But he felt an unprecedented fulfillment from it.
That feeling would haunt him for the rest of his life.
He slowly closes his eyes.
Like a true king.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: Imbecile.

steps.name: Zaaro
steps.text: You imbecile!
The giant wolf's roar reverberates through the church.
But no one is there to answer him.
After a while, he turns his gaze to the direction Leontuzzo left.
He does not accept such failure.
Absolutely not.
The streets of Volsinii are either packed with fighting famiglie, or completely empty.
Not a soul notices an old woman walking slowly over the city gate.
And not far away, a blindfolded Sankta quietly awaits her arrival.

steps.name: Genial Old Lady
steps.text: You can already see the buildings of the new city from here?

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: That's right. Spectacular, isn't it?

steps.name: Genial Old Lady
steps.text: Hah, if you ask me, the edges and corners are a bit too sharp for my liking.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: That just means your tastes are behind the times, Sicilia.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: How could yours be any better?

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: So, have you made up your mind?

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Not yet.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Let's send out warnings to the noisiest famiglie.
As Signora Sicilia's voice falls, a few black shadows spring out not too far behind her.
They quickly disappear into the buildings of Volsinii.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Then, I'd like to go see an old friend.

steps.name: Agenir
steps.text: Is my opinion alone not sufficient?

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: It's always better to get a second opinion, and a third.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: So you are here.

steps.name: Ben
steps.text: Agenir told you that, didn't he?

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Sure enough.

steps.name: Ben
steps.text: I love the food here. It's great stuff.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: It's been a while, Ben.

steps.name: Ben
steps.text: It certainly has, Sicilia.

steps.name: Ben
steps.text: What brings you here, I wonder?

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Any guesses?

steps.name: Ben
steps.text: If you just wanted to get the city back under control, you probably wouldn't come to me.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Bernardo understands the wolfpack, and his plans ultimately boil down to four words: don't rock the boat.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: He's gotten the Dodici Famiglie all bloodthirsty, and that bloodlust doesn't quench easy.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: But it's not too hard either.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: But, I heard some other things from Agenir, and would like a little input from an old friend.

steps.name: Ben
steps.text: I don't have anything in particular to say. This is a legitimate dining establishment, and it needs a new head chef. That's about it.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: I thought you'd have some feelings about the current state of Siracusa.

steps.name: Ben
steps.text: Nostalgia is also a feeling.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: You're fickle, aren't you?

steps.name: Ben
steps.text: Do you really need my opinion?

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: Not really.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: But I am interested in hearing the thoughts of a man born to civilization who's removed himself from it.

steps.name: Ben
steps.text: In every era, people are bound by the chains of the times into which they were born.

steps.name: Ben
steps.text: You don't escape from that.

steps.name: Ben
steps.text: Bernardo's ideals were an obsession born from your era.

steps.name: Ben
steps.text: He was stuck with using violence to tear it down. He couldn't get past that.

steps.name: Signora Sicilia
steps.text: What about his son?

steps.name: Ben
steps.text: Who can say? It's not like I can predict the future.

steps.name: Ben
steps.text: But you see it too, don't you?

steps.name: Ben
steps.text: We're watching the birth of a new era here.
